Subject: Billing structure for committed seats — PO requirements and discount application

Following our legal and finance review, two things we need clarified before we can issue a PO: 1) MediaCorp requires a single purchase order per fiscal quarter that references the master subscription (our procurement system won't accept one PO per invoice), and 2) Net45 is preferred by treasury—do you accept net45 on committed capacity?

Also: our procurement team needs discounts reflected on the PO line items (not just in a separate quote PDF) for auditability. Can Redwood produce a PO-friendly line-item export showing committed units, list price, discount, and net price per month?

I've attached our PO template for reference. If we can align on the invoice cadence and PO format, procurement can push the PO through next week.

Thanks,

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear summary and the template. Short answers up front: we can accept a quarterly consolidated PO that references the master agreement; we can accept Net45 for committed subscriptions (we normally default to Net30 for monthly invoices but will make an exception for committed enterprise deals); and — yes — we can provide a PO-format line-item export with discount fields populated.

A couple of implementation details:
- We prefer one PO referencing a single contract id per quarter. If MediaCorp needs a PO that spans multiple quarters we'll need separate POs (one per quarter) to match our billing cycle — that keeps invoice reconciliation straightforward.
- For committed capacity discounts (RDW-8372), discount will be applied at the subscription level and displayed as a per-line discount on the PO export.
- We can produce monthly consolidated invoices tied back to the quarterly PO (invoice numbers will include the quarter and subscription id). Example: INV-2026Q4-RDW8372-001.

I'll ask Billing to generate a sample PO export and attach the SOW with fields prefilled. Ben / Karthik — can you confirm the sample export format (CSV + PDF) and whether legal needs any PO clause changes?

Best,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Billing structure for committed seats — PO requirements and discount application

Ben / team — accounting perspective: we can keep the committed discount without requiring full prepayment by using a committed-commitment amortization model. Mechanically:
- Customer signs quarterly PO referencing the master SOW and the committed seat count.
- We bill monthly at the discounted net rate (no prepayment).
- At quarter close, we run usage reconciliation: if MediaCorp consumed fewer seats than committed, we invoice the shortfall at net (to preserve revenue recognition); if they consumed more, we invoice overage at the base list price or an agreed overage rate.

This keeps MediaCorp at Net45 monthly invoices, preserves the discount for committed seats, and avoids forcing treasury to prepay. It does require a short reconciliation invoice at quarter end in some cases.

From a legal/PO perspective there's no additional clause necessary beyond: PO must reference contract id RDW-8372 and state the quarter and billing cadence. Our AR team is comfortable with that flow.

—Karthik
